title: Correlated memory effect of environment in radical-pair magnetoreception
authors: Shixuan Chen, Yao Wang, Rui-Xue Xu, YiJing Yan
abstract: In the photoreceptor compass model, a light-generated, spin-correlated radical pair undergoes singlet-triplet interconversion driven by Zeeman and anisotropic hyperfine interactions, leading to orientation-dependent reaction yields. In this study, we consider simultaneously the spin environment and the boson environment surrounding the radical-pair system and concentrate on the correlated memory effect of the spin bath. In the linear-response limit, the spin bath is mapped to an effective Gaussian environment. The system dynamics and yields under its influence together with the bosonic bath are propagated uniformly using the hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) or equivalently the dissipaton equations of motion (DEOM) method. The HEOM/DEOM is non-Markovian and non-perturbative, exact for Gaussian environments. Corresponding results of the Markovian Lindblad master equation are also shown for comparison. Numerical demonstrations highlight the non-Markovian memory effect as a crucial ingredient for radical-pair magnetoreception.
summary: This theoretical study models radical-pair magnetoreception, treating the system as coupled to both a spin bath and a bosonic bath. By employing the non-Markovian HEOM/DEOM method, the authors demonstrate that the correlated memory effects from these environments are essential for correctly predicting the compass response. The findings highlight the limitations of simpler Markovian approximations in this context.
main_problem: The study investigates the role of the correlated memory effect from the environment in determining the efficiency of radical-pair magnetoreception.
main_result: The non-Markovian memory effect from both the spin bath and the bosonic bath is shown to be a crucial ingredient, as Markovian approximations fail to accurately predict the angular dependence of the reaction yield.
method: The dynamics are propagated using the non-Markovian Hierarchical Equations of Motion (HEOM) or Dissipative Equations of Motion (DEOM) method, comparing results against the Markovian Lindblad master equation.
model_or_system: The system is a light-generated, spin-correlated radical pair undergoing singlet-triplet interconversion, influenced by both a spin bath and a bosonic bath.
key_observables: Spin populations ($P_\alpha(t)$) and the orientation-dependent reaction yields ($\Phi_\alpha(B, 	heta)$).
important_parameters: Bath memory effect (controlled by spin-bath cutoff frequency $\omega_{sp}^c$) and the cross-correlation between bath components ($\sigma_{12}$).
main_assumptions: The spin bath is treated as an effective Gaussian environment in the linear-response limit, allowing the use of HEOM/DEOM for simultaneous non-Markovian treatment of both baths.
figures_summary: Figures compare HEOM/DEOM results against Lindblad results, demonstrating that the angular dependence of the reaction yield is highly sensitive to the inclusion of bath memory effects.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the full Hamiltonian including system, spin bath, and bosonic bath interactions. It then develops the non-Markovian HEOM/DEOM framework, compares it to the Markovian Lindblad limit, and finally presents numerical results showing the necessity of memory effects and spatial correlations for accurate magnetoreception modeling.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, non-perturbative treatment of open quantum systems involving multiple correlated baths, which is highly relevant for understanding decoherence and quantum dynamics in complex physical systems like biological sensors.
